alex: Heads-up — ran into a weird case in staging where the auto-fallback kicked in repeatedly for a single customer. Not sure if it's a policy tuning issue or a telemetry gap.

sophia: Can you paste the failure sample and the policy id?

alex: policy id: fallback.v2.rate-qos. Reason tag: "latency-window:95p" then "5xx-spike". Sample trace id: trace-5fc9. Payload snippet: `{"route":"/v1/generate","seq_len":512,"customer_id":"acme-42"}`.

jamal: thanks. Two quick things: 1) Is this the policy owned by routing-service or by decision-service? 2) Are we using the quiet-degrade mode (partial response) or hard-switchover (alt-model)?

alex: currently routing-service evaluates the rule (we pushed that change last month). It returned a soft-degrade (quiet) first, then a hard failover after three attempts.

sophia: That flow sounds right but the audit trail we show in the Console only lists the final action (hard-switchover). We need a breadcrumbed timeline: initial trigger -> sampled requests -> escalation -> operator override.

kevin: Agreed. UX ask: add a "Why we fell back" panel that shows: 1) triggering metric + window (e.g., p95 > 450ms for 2m), 2) sample request, 3) deterministic rule match, 4) elected fallback target. Minimal mockup: `Trigger: p95>450ms (2m) -> Match: fallback.v2.rate-qos -> Mode: quiet-degrade -> Escalated: hard-switchover after 3 errors`

jamal: On the infra side, we debated where to surface the sampled request payloads. If we persist full payloads in routing DB they count against retention/PII. Proposal: store only a deterministic fingerprint + hashed payload + preview fields (route, seq_len, model_family). Full replay available on-demand via a signed temporary fetch.

sophia: Love that. Also: telemetry gap — the console only shows aggregate counts by policy, not by sub-reason (latency vs 5xx vs quota). We should tag events with reason codes and surface a small stacked chart over time.

alex: Quick operational problem: the auto-escalation threshold (3 errors / 30s) was too low for this customer because they had bursty seq_len=1024 traffic. We might need customer-scoped hysteresis or a rate-normalized grace.

kevin: Could we instead make the escalation rule reference a normalized error-rate: errors_per_1000_tokens? That would reduce unfair escalations on long-request customers.

jamal: API design debate: Should the token-normalized rule be implemented as a new metric in metrics-service (recommended) or computed inline in routing-service? My vote: metrics-service — single source of truth, easier to index.

sophia: Metrics-service is fine but we need an eventual consistency contract: routing must be able to make decisions without ~10s lag. Any metric approach must guarantee a bounded staleness on the aggregation window.

alex: For the Console UX, two more things: add a "replay this sample" button that triggers a sandbox replay with the same routing decisions, and a small "operator action" timeline where you can mark "accepted" or "reverted". Those actions should create audit-events we can query.

kevin: Replay should be gated (rbac + signed token). Also include an opt-out flag for payloads that contain sensitive fields.

jamal: Implementation plan sketch: 1) Add reason-code labels to fallback events (latency, 5xx, quota, mismatch). 2) Extend routing events with fingerprint + preview fields. 3) Metrics-service publishes normalized-error-rate. 4) Console UI: breadcrumb timeline + replay + operator action buttons.

sophia: Timeline + reason breakdown are non-negotiable for the next sprint. Can we prod an initial API spec? Keep it minimal: `/v1/fallback-events?policy_id=...&from=...&to=...` returns list of event summaries with `reason_code`, `mode`, `sample_preview`, `action_history` (no payload). Full payload fetch: `/v1/fallback-events/{id}/replay-token` -> returns short-lived URL for replay (rbac check).

alex: That API shape looks good. jamal — can you mock up the DB schema changes for event summaries (fingerprint, preview fields, reason_code, mode, escalation_count, action_history_ids)? Keep everything as small strings/ints.

jamal: Will do. I'll also add an integration test that simulates a long-seq customer to ensure hysteresis works.

kevin: One last edge: operator override should be able to pin a route to a slower fallback for X minutes (escape hatch). That should be an immutable audit event with owner and TTL.

sophia: Good. alex — can you open a Console ticket with the mock copy and a short Figma link? I'll pair with product to prioritize.

alex: Opening ticket now: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/PLAT-1129. Figma: https://figma.com/s/console-fallback-timeline (mock).

devops-bot: Deployment note: routing-service v1.24.3 includes fallback.v2 evaluation. Rolling to staging now (canary 10%).

alex: Great — thanks all. Let's sync tomorrow after staging canary completes and we have a sample replay.

sophia: Thanks — will add to the eng sync agenda. :thumbsup:
